acceptance: An upstream pull request for the reduced sqlite-date-day-arithmetic change is opened and linked; patches.json moves sqlite-date-day-arithmetic to upstream_state offered with that tobymao/sqlglot URL and a reason saying where it stands.
The upstream PR's tests pass locally and in upstream CI, with the evidence recorded in context.
context:
Decision gate (owner): approved 2026-11-19 by Joe Harris (choice dialog) for an upstream offer to tobymao/sqlglot.

Verification rubric: (1) the reduced change applies to current upstream main and stands alone, without the fork patches it stacks on; (2) its dialect tests pass, with execution checked on real SQLite; (3) the fork's downstream contract tests pass after the patches.json edit.

Guardrails: the offered change is the fork patch reduced to upstream-only behaviour with no benchbox package references; one change per PR; the patch stays carried in patches.json until upstream merges and a refresh retires it with equivalence evidence.

Upstream rules (tobymao/sqlglot AGENTS.md): Conventional Commits title ending with [CLAUDE]; minimal scope; tests in tests/dialects.
description: SQLite DATEDIFF in DAY units round trip, without an unsupported warning (upstream v30.31.0 already lowers DATE_SUB). No BenchBox-specific behaviour. In the fork it stacks on sqlite-temporal-lowering, which upstream declined, so the offer needs a standalone version against upstream main.
drop_reason: Nothing to offer: upstream main (7d21ccc1) already writes DATEDIFF ... DAY for SQLite without an unsupported warning, and test_datediff covers it; the fork patch only adds an equivalent branch and can retire at the next refresh (recorded in BenchBox-dev/benchbox-sqlglot#120). A separate upstream bug found while checking (DAY truncates elapsed time instead of counting day boundaries) was filed as https://github.com/tobymao/sqlglot/issues/9271 with owner approval on 2026-11-19.
